faq.title: Questions Before Getting Started?
faq.desc: Find answers about our engineering services, project enquiries, BIM automation, confidentiality and private-access opportunities.
faq.contact_prompt: Still have a question? Contact our team.
faq.a1: pyBIM supports engineering and AEC teams with BIM modeling, Scan-to-BIM, model coordination, digital delivery workflows and targeted automation. The scope of each engagement is defined around project requirements, available documentation and technical deliverables. Explore our complete range on the Services page.
faq.q2: What information should I provide for a project enquiry?
faq.a2: Start with the project type, current stage, required services, engineering disciplines, expected deliverables and indicative timeline. Details such as model formats, BIM requirements and existing project documentation can help us assess the scope more effectively. You can share these details directly in our Project Enquiry form.
faq.q3: Can pyBIM collaborate with international engineering teams?
faq.a3: pyBIM can discuss remote and cross-border collaboration with engineering firms, architects and BIM teams. Project delivery arrangements, coordination workflows, applicable standards and communication requirements are agreed according to the scope and location of each engagement.
faq.q4: How do you handle confidential project information?
faq.a4: Confidentiality requirements can be reviewed before sensitive project information is shared. Where appropriate, we can discuss nondisclosure agreements, access restrictions and project-specific data-handling arrangements. The applicable protections depend on the agreed scope, systems and delivery model.
faq.q5: How does the BIM Automation ROI Matrix work?
faq.a5: The ROI Matrix uses operational assumptions such as team size, hourly labor cost, repetitive-work hours and working weeks to structure potential automation scenarios. Its outputs are estimates rather than guaranteed savings. Access to the full workbook is subject to the applicable review and delivery process. You can evaluate your baseline parameters in the ROI Matrix section.
faq.q6: How can my company apply for Phase II private access?
faq.a6: Complete the Private Access application with your organization details, technical environment, deployment preferences and intended use. Phase II is currently being evaluated with selected companies and trusted professionals in controlled private environments. New applications are reviewed individually, and submission does not guarantee acceptance. You can submit your requirements in the Private Access section.
faq.q7: When is Phase II expected to become more widely available?
faq.a7: The current target window for the next Phase II release stage is Q2–Q4 2027. This is an indicative planning window and may change as development, integration testing, reliability checks and security validation continue. Private access opportunities are managed separately through the application process.
faq.q8: What happens after I submit an enquiry or application?
faq.a8: Project enquiries and Phase II private-access applications follow separate review processes. Where a submission is successfully received, the relevant team can assess the information provided and determine appropriate next steps. Follow-up depends on the nature of the request, and submitting an application does not guarantee access or a response within a fixed timeframe.
roi.section.title: Estimate the Impact of BIM Automation.
roi.section.desc: Explore how repetitive BIM workflows affect engineering capacity and operational costs, and assess the potential value of targeted automation.
roi.narrative.problem_desc: Manual coordination, repetitive data entry and fragmented BIM workflows consume valuable engineering time.
roi.narrative.impact_desc: Recurring operational tasks can reduce delivery capacity, increase coordination overhead and limit the time available for higher-value engineering work.
roi.narrative.solution_desc: Targeted automation using tools such as Revit scripting, Python and C# can streamline repetitive operations and support more consistent digital delivery.
roi.deliverables.title: What the Matrix Delivers
roi.deliverables.d1_desc: Estimate how repetitive BIM tasks contribute to time and cost overhead.
roi.deliverables.d2_desc: Compare conservative, expected and optimized adoption assumptions.
roi.deliverables.d3_desc: Use structured financial estimates to inform conversations about automation priorities.
roi.citation.title: Autodesk Industry Reference
roi.citation.finding: Surveyed construction roles spend an average of 13 hours per person each week finding project data.
roi.citation.source_title: Autodesk, 2025 State of Design & Make: Spotlight on Construction.
roi.citation.disclaimer: The 13-hour figure represents an industry reference for general time spent finding data across surveyed construction roles. It does not measure isolated BIM modeling inefficiency, is not verified modeler waste, and should not be assumed to be 100% recoverable.
roi.inputs.hourly_rate_help: Optional illustrative consulting baseline (€85/h example). Valuates capacity at external market billing potential. Leave blank to use the €85/h example, or enter your organization's custom billing rate.
roi.inputs.hourly_rate_internal_help: Internal employee labor cost (gross salary + employer taxes + pensions + overheads). Please supply your actual internal loaded labor cost. Billing capacity potential and internal payroll savings are not aggregated.
roi.inputs.search_finding_data: Locating project data across construction roles
roi.inputs.search_benchmark_desc: Fixed 13 hrs/wk Autodesk 2025 study observation across construction roles. Locked standard scenario reference.
roi.inputs.region_help: Contextual baseline reference only. Selecting a region provides market context and will never overwrite your entered rate.
roi.inputs.hours_search_help: Fixed 13 hrs/wk reference based on Autodesk's 2025 State of Design & Make study across construction roles.
roi.inputs.working_weeks_help: Editable initial planning assumption (excluding leave and holidays), not a European legal or statistical standard.
roi.advanced.title: Advanced Workflow Assessment
roi.advanced.desc: Diagnostic assessment across 4 distinct categories. Category 4 protects non-automatable engineering judgment. The standard scenario model remains locked to the 13h benchmark to prevent double-counting.
roi.advanced.cat_search_desc: Locating drawings, querying models, verifying revisions across CDEs.
roi.advanced.cat_entry_desc: Parameter population, schedule editing, manual title block and sheet updates.
roi.advanced.cat_discipline_desc: Clash grouping and triage, dynamic QTO syncing, IFC property audits.
roi.advanced.cat_judgment_desc: Creative design, structural deliberation, client problem-solving, architectural decision-making. Preserved and excluded from automation recovery.
roi.advanced.reconciliation_note: Reconciliation Active: Weekly repetitive hours for automation preview are calculated as (1 + 2 + 3). Category 4 is protected.
roi.advanced.overlap_warning: Note: The 60-hour/week cap acts as a structural sanity check against impossible individual weekly totals, but does not by itself guarantee absence of semantic overlap. Please ensure tasks are distinctly categorized across search, entry, and modeling.
roi.preview.status_note: Five Fixed AI Adoption Scenarios with 10% Engineering Verification Allowance
roi.preview.paused_desc: Please provide valid operational inputs above (at least 1 modeler, valid positive rate if custom, valid working weeks) to calculate illustrative scenarios.
roi.preview.paused_internal_rate: Please enter your internal loaded labor cost (€ / hour) to calculate scenario estimates.
roi.preview.annual_repetitive_desc: Total annual team hours allocated to routine, repetitive tasks.
roi.preview.disclaimer: All figures represent an illustrative capacity valuation based on customer-selected planning inputs and the Autodesk 13h/wk industry reference. Figures do NOT represent guaranteed revenue, net profit, direct cash savings, payroll cost reductions, or software sales warranties.

roi.access.eligible_desc: Your browser download has been initiated. If the file did not appear automatically, please check your browser download manager. Unlocked cells can be edited in Microsoft Excel or compatible spreadsheet software to recalculate outputs dynamically.
roi.access.stateless_notice: Stateless verification receipt: Submissions are NOT durably stored or emailed to recipients. Client-side download gating is for UX guidance only and does not represent an access-controlled security barrier. File creation does not prove local filesystem save.
roi.access.privacy_disclosure: Corporate verification notice: Submitted business contact details are processed to verify corporate eligibility and dispatch an internal lead notification to pyBIM Support (support@pybim.com). Domain MX checks verify mail-exchange routing but do not prove mailbox ownership. Submissions are not added to marketing lists and imply no unsolicited marketing opt-in.
